fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Producer Price Index, which measures the prices US producers receive for their output. It is read as a leading signal for consumer inflation, since input and wholesale costs eventually reach retail prices.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, released around the middle of the following month. It is the earliest broad read on consumer spending, which drives roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's governing council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the euro area. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across twenty economies and shape the euro's value against every other currency.
ecb-2026-09.recent: This decision comes after a run of holds elsewhere: the Bank of England kept rates at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers dissenting, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and the RBA held steady. The dollar has fallen to its lowest level since May.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move borrowing costs across the dollar economy and price every asset quoted against the dollar.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The committee meets with the dollar at its weakest since May and gold near $4,392 an ounce, and with Trump moving a second time to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. The Bank of England held at 3.75% with three of nine dissenting and the Bank of Japan held at 1%, leaving the Fed the outlier still to decide.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which sets Bank Rate for the United Kingdom at eight scheduled meetings a year. Its votes set the cost of sterling borrowing, from mortgages to gilt yields, and are published with each member's position.
boe-2026-09.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July, waiting to see the impact of the Iran war, and three of nine policymakers voted to raise. That split is what this meeting inherits. UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates, and the dollar fell to its lowest level since May with a rate hike in doubt.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of yen funding, which anchors the yen's exchange rate and the global carry trades built on cheap Japanese money.
boj-2026-09.recent: The Bank of Japan held at 1% on 31 July while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before that decision. The US then joined a historic joint intervention on 3 August, and the dollar fell to its lowest level since May. This meeting is the board's first rate call since that coordination.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, published by the Office for National Statistics, measuring how much prices paid by households have changed over the past year. It is the reference number for Bank of England rate decisions, index-linked gilts, and a range of benefits and rail fares.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The release lands as inflation data drives markets elsewhere: India's retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June on food prices, and crypto traders moved around US CPI day, with bitcoin near $63,500. This print will set the annual UK rate the Bank of England weighs at its next meeting.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy, and with it assets priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets with its own composition in dispute: Trump is trying again to fire Cook, reviving the Fed independence fight. The dollar has already fallen to its weakest since May with a rate hike in doubt, gold hit $4,392 an ounce, and other central banks have split — three of nine BoE policymakers voted to raise.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets policy rates for the euro area's twenty economies. Its decisions transmit through bank lending across the bloc and set the euro's yield against the dollar and the yen.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision comes after a run of holds at the major central banks: the Bank of England held at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers voting to raise, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and the RBA held as its housing market softened. The dollar has fallen to its lowest level since May.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank sets the country's policy rate, with its board meeting roughly eight times a year. Its decisions drive the yen, Japanese government bond yields, and the cheap-funding trades built on decades of near-zero Japanese rates.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan held at 1% on 31 July while warning that underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before that decision. Days later Japan confirmed a historic joint yen intervention with the US. This meeting is the first test of whether rates, rather than intervention, carry the yen.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, whose nine members vote to set Bank Rate, the benchmark for borrowing across the UK economy. Its decisions transmit to mortgages, business credit and sterling.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July with three of nine voting to raise, a split that leaves the next decision genuinely open. It held while waiting to see the impact of the Iran war on supply, and UK house prices rose just 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates. November settles whether that pause holds.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy, and with it every asset priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The dollar fell to its weakest since May as a rate hike came into doubt, and gold hit $4,392 an ounce. Trump has moved again to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. The BOJ held at 1% while three of nine Bank of England policymakers voted to raise, leaving the committee split against a divided global backdrop.
